description_en: Bhaiṣajyarāja Bāhāḥ, a branch of the Cikã Bahī (Saptapura Mahāvihāra,LAL1620), is located behind a five-bayedphalcāat the junction of the street from Bhelāchẽ and Bhindyaḥ Sataḥ at Cyāsal. The entrance to this Bāhāḥ is on a boundary wall to the west and it is attached to aphalcāto its south. The main structure is divided into three small rooms, consisting of a central sanctum room and two small rooms on either side. A small staircase in the eastern room leads up to the upper floor. The building shares a small space with a single-storey annex structure to its north.The courtyard measures 7 m × 4.7 m, and has a residential building to the its east and north. Both of these are built on arcadedphalcāsthat serve as the ground floor. Acaityasits to the north of theBāhāḥ, directly in front of its main door. The courtyard is paved withteliatiles. Small images of different Buddhist deities have been placed on the walls of the southern annex building and western boundary wall.Jīvanṛsiṃha, a member of the Cikã Bahī and an Āyurvedic doctor (vaidya) by profession, established this Bāhāḥ in 1878 (NS 998). It takes its name from Jīvanṛsiṃha's profession; hence, it is known as Bhaiṣajyarāja Bāhāḥ. Wall paintings of the Five Buddhas can be found above the plain outer entrance,which is flanked by paintings of auspicious symbols. The north-facing god house has two storeys and a tiled roof supported by plain struts. Instead of a pinnacle, a small chimney (bhaipvāḥ) can be found on its sloping roof, as well as three metal banners displaying images of deities. The first floor of the god house is very low.There is notoraṇaabove the carved door of the sanctum, though it is flanked by two stone lions as it is customary. The lions also sit next to two metal flags that were donated in 1909 (NS 1023). The main facade of the god-house was decorated with wall paintings of various deities, but the old plaster is now crumbling away, making most of the paintings unrecognizable. Inside the sanctum, one can find a north-facing stone image of Akṣobhya.
description_ne: चिकंबहीको दक्षिणतिर अवस्थित यो भैषज्यराज बाहा:, चिकंबही (सप्तपुर महाविहार) को शाखा हो । यो विहार चिकंबहीका वैद्य जीवनृसिंहले १८७८ (नेसं ९९८) मा स्थापना गरेका हुन् । वैद्यले स्थापना गरेको हुनाले यसलाई भैषज्यराज बाहा: भनिएको हो । सामान्य ढोकाबाट भित्र छिरेपछि सानो चोकको दक्षिण छेउमा यो विहार रहेको छ । विहारको दुईतले द्य:छेँ उत्तराभिमुख छ र छाना झिँगटीले छाइएको छ । छानामा गजुर छैन तर धुवाँ निस्कने सानो भौप्वा: राखिएको छ । छानालाई अड्याउन सादा टुँडाल राखिएका छन् । छानामा बौद्ध देवीहरू अंकित तीनवटा हलंपौ झुण्ड्याइएको छ । पहिले चारवटा हलंपौ भएकोमा अहिले तीनवटा मात्र बाँकी छन् । पहिलो तला निकै होचो बनाइएको छ । भुइँतल्लामा उत्तराभिमुख गरी अक्षोभ्यको ढुंगाको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकामाथि तोरण छैन तर ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ एक जोडी ढुंगाको सिंहमूर्ति छन् । ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ कालक्रमले गर्दा जीर्ण भइसकेका भित्तेचित्रहरू देखिन्छन् । सिंहको दायाँ-बायाँ नेसं १०२३ मा चढाइएका धातुको झण्डा राखिएका छन् ।विहार परिसरमा एउटा धर्मधातु जिनालय चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । विहारको पूर्वतिरको भित्तामा गणेश र महाकाल स्थापना गरिएका छन् भने पश्चिमतिरको भित्तामा मञ्जुश्री, भीमसेन र गरुड राखिएका छन् ।

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a pair of metal flags
historical_events.event_description: Kulamānasingh, Ratnamāna and Gaṇeśa Bahādur donated a pair of flags to Akṣobhya.

Jīvanṛsiṃha, a member of the Cikã Bahī, established this Bāhāḥ together with thecaityain 1878 (NS 998). He wished that his father Bhājudhana and mother Mayju Thakunī would dwell in the Sukhāvatī Bhuvana. Jīvanṛsiṃha was supported by his stepmother Dhana Thakunī, his wife Lakṣmī Thakunī, his sons Kulamāna Siṃha, Ratnamāna Siṃha, Kulabahādura Siṃha, Gaṇeśabahādura Siṃha, and his daughter Yogamāyā.
